subject: Post-discovery: SDK onboarding + tool-specs for multi-tool rerank POC
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-08-19T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-discovery: SDK onboarding + tool-specs for multi-tool rerank POC

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Recap (short):
- Goal: replace current keyword-ranking flow with a hybrid embedding + rerank pipeline that can call external enrichment tools (billing check, patient-matching) and fall back to a fast heuristic when services are slow.
- Success metric for POC: 10–15% lift in relevant results (A/B) and end-to-end 200ms 95th pct latency for cached queries.

Technical asks we discussed:
1) SDK onboarding: you said engineering can accept an SDK + short integration guide. I attached a compact quickstart (kimberly-sdk-quickstart.pdf).
2) Auth & routing: we recommended token-based service accounts with mTLS optional; detailed routing rules (region-aware + model-cost policy) to be agreed.
3) Tool definitions: we sketched three tool types — enrichment, 3rd-party lookup, and side-effect actions — and will provide a YAML manifest for your ops team (tool-defs-v1.yaml attached).
4) Embeddings/reranker: we propose embeddings for recall (dense retriever) + a two-stage reranker (fast lightweight model for initial sort, larger cross-encoder for top-K).

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- Brightline engineering: share a test service account and one representative API endpoint for enrichment (Alex / Priya) — target by Tue 8/21.
- Redwood: internal engineering (Aditya + Vivek) will draft an integration checklist (auth, rate limits, retry policy, observable spans) and a skeleton SDK adapter — deliver Wed 8/21 EOD.
- Schedule a 30-minute POC kickoff demo (hands-on) for Thu 8/22 or Fri 8/23 — propose Thu 8/22 10am PT.

Notes on error-handling & graceful degradation (quick):
- Use soft-fail semantics for enrichment tools (return null + telemetry).
- Implement parallel calls for non-dependent tools (run enrichment + billing check concurrently) with an aggregator that merges results and annotates confidence.
- If cross-encoder times out, fallback to cached lightweight scorer and tag result with "fallback=true" in structured output so product can surface it differently.

I cc'd Aditya so he can add any integration constraints we should be aware of (esp. SDK side: language targets, runtime, and minimal footprint).

Thanks — Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Kimberly — appreciate the concise recap. Priya and I reviewed with eng. A few clarifications and constraints from our side:

1) Network/security: our infra team requires outbound TLS 1.3 + pinning to a set of IP ranges or a private endpoint via GRE tunnel. I've attached our network checklist (brightline-network-requirements.xlsx).
2) Auth: service accounts are fine; we prefer JWT-based short-lived tokens minted by our identity broker (we can add Redwood as an audience).
3) Sandbox data: we can provide a reproducible sample corpus and a test enrichment endpoint (returns synthetic patient metadata) — target to share on Tue 8/21.

On tools: the enrichment tool will be idempotent but occasionally 500s during load. We need a recommended retry/backoff pattern and a way to tag stale enrichment data.

We can do Thu 8/22 10am PT for the kickoff. Please send an invite and the agenda.

Thanks — Alex

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-08-20T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: SDK onboarding + tool-specs for multi-tool rerank POC

Adding engineering notes and a short integration plan.

Platform constraints / assumptions:
- Primary SDK targets: Node (server), Python 3.11, and a lightweight Go client if needed. We will avoid heavy native deps so embedded users (serverless) can adopt quickly.
- Auth: support bearer JWT and mTLS. SDK will include automatic token refresh + optional local caching of short-lived tokens.
- Routing/levers: SDK exposes a routing policy object: {latencyBudgetMs, costTier, preferredModel, regionHint}. The platform enforces policies server-side but SDK provides hints.

Tool definition proposal (high level):
- tool_id: enrichment.patient_profile
  type: enrichment
  contract: input: {patient_id}, output: {profile:{age,gender,flags}}
  timeout_ms: 250
  retry_policy: [50ms, 150ms, 400ms] (only on 5xx)
  fallbacks: null

- tool_id: external.billing_check
  type: lookup
  contract: input: {account_id}, output: {balance,status}
  timeout_ms: 180
  retry_policy: [30ms, 100ms]
  fallbacks: stubbed_status

- tool_id: side.effect.schedule_message
  type: action
  contract: input: {phone,message}, output: {task_id}
  timeout_ms: 600
  retry_policy: single-no-retry (idempotency handled by caller)

Parallelization & orchestration:
- Non-dependent tools run in parallel with a bounded concurrency pool. Collector merges results and attaches tool-level latency and error codes into the structured output: {tools:[{tool_id, status, latency_ms, payload}]}.
- Aggregator will compute a lightweight confidence score combining tool latencies, missing fields, and model score; attach to final reranker input.

Error-handling patterns:
- Soft-fail: enrichment returns null; we tag downstream input with missing_enrichment=true.
- Fast-fallback: if cross-encoder times out, return the lightweight reranker output and annotate fallback_reason and fallback_model_version.
- Observability: emit spans for each tool call, include request_id and token hashes; expose last-success timestamps for each tool in the admin UI.

Deliverables by Wed 8/21 EOD:
- public: SDK adapter repo skeleton + README, small code samples (node/python).
- internal: a small integration test harness that runs the pipeline against Brightline sample data and simulates tool failures.

I can pair with Priya/Alex on Wed afternoon if they want a run-through of the adapter.

—Aditya
Lead Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
